database_summary: This is a small dimensional-style dataset about fictional superheroes. Core entity is superhero (one row per hero) with descriptive attributes (name, physical attributes, demographic ids, publisher, alignment). Lookup/dimension tables provide enumerations for gender, colour (eyes/hair/skin), race, publisher, alignment, attribute (like Intelligence) and superpower. Junction tables hero_attribute (numeric attribute values per hero/attribute) and hero_power (many-to-many hero <-> superpower) capture measurements/events/assignments. Row counts indicate a single snapshot of heroes and many-to-many relationships; there is no temporal/version history in the schema.

accepted.name: hero_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  superhero_name,
  full_name,
  gender_id,
  eye_colour_id,
  hair_colour_id,
  skin_colour_id,
  race_id,
  publisher_id,
  alignment_id,
  height_cm,
  weight_kg
FROM superhero
accepted.description: Normalized one-row-per-hero projection including core descriptive columns and physical measures. Use this as the canonical superhero row for joins and downstream analytics. | Use for: List heroes with their basic attributes; Filter heroes by publisher/gender/alignment/race; Compute aggregates (avg height/weight) per demographic group

accepted.name: hero_demographics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id,
  s.superhero_name,
  s.full_name,
  s.gender_id,
  gender.gender AS gender,
  s.eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.race_id,
  race.race AS race,
  s.publisher_id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.alignment_id,
  alignment.alignment AS alignment,
  s.height_cm,
  s.weight_kg
FROM superhero AS s
LEFT JOIN gender ON s.gender_id = gender.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
LEFT JOIN race ON s.race_id = race.id
LEFT JOIN publisher ON s.publisher_id = publisher.id
LEFT JOIN alignment ON s.alignment_id = alignment.id
accepted.description: Denormalized hero rows enriched with human-readable dimension labels (gender, colours, race, publisher, alignment). Useful when presenting hero attributes or grouping by these labels. | Use for: Show hero names with readable demographics and publisher; Group heroes by publisher, alignment, race, or colour; Filter heroes by human-readable attributes (e.g., alignment = 'Good')

accepted.name: hero_attribute_values
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id,
  ha.attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute AS ha
LEFT JOIN attribute ON ha.attribute_id = attribute.id
accepted.description: One row per (hero_id, attribute_id) with the attribute name and value. Use for aggregations across attributes or to pivot attributes per hero. | Use for: Find heroes' values for a given attribute (e.g., Intelligence); Compute average attribute_value by attribute_name or by hero; Pivot attributes to have one row per hero with multiple attribute columns

accepted.name: hero_power_assignments
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id,
  hp.power_id,
  superpower.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power AS hp
LEFT JOIN superpower ON hp.power_id = superpower.id
accepted.description: One row per hero-power assignment including the superpower name. Useful for counting powers per hero or listing heroes who have a given power. | Use for: List powers for a given hero; Count number of powers per hero; Find heroes who have a specific power_name

accepted.name: hero_power_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id,
  COUNT(*) AS power_count
FROM hero_power AS hp
GROUP BY hp.hero_id
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of powers per hero (one row per hero). Exposes power_count so downstream queries can filter top-N or join counts to hero details. | Use for: Rank heroes by number of powers; Filter heroes who have at least one power (power_count > 0); Compute distributions of power_count by publisher or alignment

accepted.name: hero_attribute_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id,
  COUNT(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_count,
  AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_mean,
  MIN(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_min,
  MAX(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_max,
  SUM(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_sum
FROM hero_attribute AS ha
GROUP BY ha.hero_id
accepted.description: Summary statistics per hero across their attributes: attribute_count, attribute_mean, attribute_min, attribute_max, attribute_sum. Use to compare overall attribute profiles between heroes. | Use for: Compare heroes by average attribute value; Filter heroes with many or few measured attributes; Combine attribute summary with hero demographics to find patterns

accepted.name: hero_power_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pc.hero_id,
  pc.power_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC) AS power_count_rank,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC) AS power_count_row_num
FROM (
  SELECT
    hp.hero_id,
    COUNT(*) AS power_count
  FROM hero_power AS hp
  GROUP BY hp.hero_id
) AS pc
accepted.description: Rank heroes by number of powers (dense rank and row_number available). Useful for top-N hero selection by power_count without baking a limit. | Use for: Select top-N heroes by number of powers (WHERE power_count_rank <= K); Break ties using row number or present dense ranks; Join rank to hero details to show leaders

accepted.name: heroes_with_attributes_and_powers
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  hb.id AS id,
  hb.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  hb.full_name AS full_name,
  hb.gender_id AS gender_id,
  hb.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  hb.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  hb.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  hb.race_id AS race_id,
  hb.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  hb.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  ha.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  COALESCE(pc.power_count, 0) AS power_count,
  hb.height_cm AS height_cm,
  hb.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero AS hb
LEFT JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON hb.id = ha.hero_id
LEFT JOIN attribute ON ha.attribute_id = attribute.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS power_count
  FROM hero_power
  GROUP BY hero_id
) AS pc ON hb.id = pc.hero_id
accepted.description: Wide denormalized relation: one row per hero-attribute combination enriched with hero details and power_count. Useful for analyses that need a hero's demographic context together with an attribute measurement and their power count. | Use for: Analyze relationships between attribute values and number of powers; Filter heroes by demographic traits and inspect their attribute scores; Prepare data for pivoting attributes while keeping hero measures
